question: In covering a distance of 52 km, Pranay takes 7 hours more than Aman. If Pranay doubles his speed, then he would take 6 hours less than Aman. Pranay's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When speed is doubled, the time taken is halved.

Let Pranay's original time be T. Time saved by doubling his speed = T − T/2 = T/2.

Total time saved = 7 hours (more than Aman originally) + 6 hours (less than Aman now) = 13 hours.

⇒ T/2 = 13 hours ⇒ T = 26 hours.

Pranay's original speed = Distance ÷ Time = 52 ÷ 26 = 2 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 52 km

Pranay's original time is 7 hours more than Aman's time.

When Pranay doubles his speed, his time becomes 6 hours less than Aman's time.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed × Time = Constant

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Aman's time be t.

⇒ Pranay's normal time = t + 7

⇒ Since time is inversely proportional to speed, doubling the speed will halve the time taken.

⇒ Pranay's new time = (t + 7) ÷ 2

⇒ According to the second condition, Pranay's new time = t − 6

⇒ (t + 7) ÷ 2 = t − 6

⇒ t + 7 = 2t − 12

⇒ t = 19 hours (Aman's original time)

⇒ Pranay's normal time = 19 + 7 = 26 hours

⇒ Pranay's original speed = 52 ÷ 26 = 2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

For a constant distance, speed and time are inversely proportional. The ratio of speeds S₁ : S₂ implies the ratio of times is S₂ : S₁.

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds. In opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds.

Average Speed

Average speed for a whole journey is Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds A and B, the average speed is 2AB ÷ (A + B).
